catalog_quote: [p.33, sec. 4.2 PWB phonological word] Most WB languages are sesquisyllabic-a word may consist of one or one and a half syllables. In the latter case a stressed mainsyllable is preceded by a minorsyllable, a structurally impoverished unit that is constructed from a restricted set of segments. The minorsyllable typically consists of an oral stop or fricative of unmarked phonation type, an epenthetic ([a] or schwa-like) vowel, and may be c losed by a nasal or rhotic . [p.34] Sesquisyllabism is typical for Bahnaric (and many other MK languages), and therefore it seems reasonable to assume it for PWB. ... This leads us to suppose that the phonological word in PWB was restricted to the following possibilities: Type 1: C(R)V(F) Type 2: C;}.RV(F) Type 3: C(r/n).CV(F) [p.20, sec. 3.4 Su'] Sidwell collected a 500+ wordlist, and some pages of grammar notes ... Linguistically Su' has the following notable features. ... M inorsyl lables are faithfully preserved, as in Brao (e.g. tarkool ' knee', harpiat ' tongue' etc), yet there are no lenitions of either minorsyllable or mainsyllable initials [p.21] Minorsyllables are robustly preserved, including r and n codas. There i s a strong tendency for the minorsyllable vowel to be pronounced as a distinct [a], particularly in those etyma where it is phonemic.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Su' words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables (minor syllable + main syllable); the main syllable, which is always word-final, carries the stress and the preceding minor syllable (with epenthetic/reduced vowel) is unstressed -- i.e. word-final (iambic) stress. Note this is stated for West Bahnaric languages as a group in a comparative handbook whose Su' data are Sidwell's own 2002 fieldnotes; the Su' profile itself confirms that Su' keeps full minor syllables but contains no separate stress sentence.
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress. Su' minor-syllable vowel tends to be a distinct [a], 'particularly in those etyma where it is phonemic' (p.21); minor syllables may be closed by r or n (tarkool, harpiat).
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (citation forms from a fieldwork wordlist); statement is a branch-level (West Bahnaric) generalisation, not an instrumental or Su'-specific analysis.
new_statements.identity_note: Statement source describes Su' (= Sou, Souq, autonym [ɟruʔ]) of Ban Chanto / route 18, Sanamxay district, Attapeu, Laos (Sidwell 2002 fieldwork) = Glottolog souu1238, ISO sqq. Beware homonyms: 'Souei/Souai/Suai' in Huffman's notebooks and in Champasak/Salavan is Kuy (Katuic, kuy 1252 group), and L-Thongkum's Xekong 'Suai' is Juk (West Bahnaric, jukk1234?) -- neither is this language. The stress sentence quoted is a West-Bahnaric-wide generalisation (sec. 4.2), applied to Su' via the Su' profile's statement that minor syllables are fully preserved.
